questionText: Shall an act, passed at the 2026 session of the General Assembly, entitled “An Act authorizing the City of Cranston to finance the repair, construction, and rehabilitation of storm drains and drainage improvements, and the remediation and mitigation of drainage and flooding problems, by the issuance of not more than $4,000,000 general obligation bonds and notes therefor” be approved?
officialStatement:

Additionally, funds will be used to purchase equipment and resources to clean catch basins, as well as other water quality structures, as mandated by the RI DEM Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System (MS4) General Permit. The goal of the program is to reduce the quantity of pollutants that enter storm sewer systems during storm events.
$4,000,000 will be borrowed. The repair, construction, and rehabilitation of storm drains and drainage improvements may begin in 2027 and may be completed in approximately 10 years. Although each asset has a different useful life, the average useful life of the drainage improvements is approximately 40 years.

Explanation of voter referenda questions on Cranston's 2026 General Election ballot:
A referendum is the way our legislative bodies (the General Assembly or City Council) ask voters to approve or reject proposals such as constitutional amendments, home rule charter amendments, long-term borrowings (bonds), and special laws affecting the city. Voter information regarding Cranston’s local referenda is included in this pamphlet.
Approve: Your vote to “Approve” means that you support the city issuing General Obligation Bonds to finance the projects listed in a specified local bond question. If a majority of Cranston voters voting on the question vote to approve, that question will be certified by the Cranston Board of Canvassers as having passed. Bonding authority related to that question will be granted, however, approval of a bond question does not itself result in the issuance of bonds or the expenditure of funds. Any future issuance of bonds and expenditure of bond proceeds would require action by the city, including the Mayor and City Council, as provided by law.
Reject: Your vote to “Reject” means that you are opposed to the city issuing General Obligation Bonds to finance the projects listed in a specified local bond question. If a majority of Cranston voters voting on the question vote to reject, that question will be certified by the Cranston Board of Canvassers as having been rejected, and no bonding authority related to that question will be granted.

Reject: Your vote to “Reject” means that you are opposed to the city issuing General Obligation Bonds to finance the projects listed in a specified local bond question. questionText: Shall an act, passed at the 2026 session of the General Assembly, entitled “An Act authorizing the City of Cranston to finance the design, construction, repair, rehabilitation, and improvement of streets, sidewalks, and bridges in the city including, but not limited to, paving, drainage, traffic control devices, road maintenance equipment, safety improvements, and landscaping and all costs incidental or related thereto by the issuance of not more than $8,000,000 general obligation bonds and notes therefor” be approved?
officialStatement:
Explanation and purpose of Question 9: These bonds will be used to finance the design, construction, repair, rehabilitation, and improvement of streets, sidewalks, and bridges in the city. This may include, but is not limited to, paving, drainage, traffic control devices, road maintenance equipment, safety improvements, and landscaping. Projects may also include Dyer Ave./Park Ave. intersection improvements, the Hope Rd. - Wilbur Rd. - Phenix Ave. roundabout, main street beautification (Park Ave. improvements), and traffic signal upgrades.
